title: Sensible defaults for cache tiers and conservative quantization safety layer
author: Priya Singh
release_notes: Added conservative runtime defaults for cache tiers, a safety wrapper for automatic low-bit quantization rollouts, and a unit-econ delta report generator. No behavioral breaking changes for existing tenants; new opt-ins available for aggressive optimization.
description:
Motivation: customers increasingly enable aggressive quantization and cache trimming via automated profiles; we observed regressions in perceptual-quality sensitive flows and noisy unit-econ signals when defaults allowed too-aggressive rollouts. This PR introduces conservative, production-friendly defaults for cache tiers and a quantization safety layer that prevents automatic low-bit rollouts in high-risk contexts.

What this changes (summary):
- Introduces a tiered cache defaults module (packages/runtime/src/cache/defaults.ts) with conservative TTLs, explicit warmup thresholds, and a tenant opt-in flag for more aggressive caching. Defaults are chosen to reduce tail-latency variance while preserving unit-econ improvement potential.
- Adds a quantization safety wrapper (packages/runtime/src/quantization/safety-layer.ts) which annotates model variants with a safety_score (string label + float) and blocks auto-rollout to <8-bit quantized variants for inputs flagged as quality-sensitive (e.g., code generation, long-form summarization). The safety policy is configurable via the optimization-settings UI.
- Console UI: new control in tenant optimization settings to opt into aggressive defaults, and a visual indicator showing quantization risk (packages/console/src/components/tenants/optimization-settings.tsx).
- CLI: unit-econ diff command (packages/cli/src/commands/unit-econ-diff.ts) which produces a compact report comparing token-level cost deltas and sample-quality regressions between a baseline and a candidate config. This helps SREs and PMs validate that default changes produce net-positive unit economics.
- Tests: added integration e2e tests that simulate a high-quality workload and verify the safety-layer blocks unsafe rollouts (integration-tests/e2e/quant-safety.spec.ts) and caching fixture (integration-tests/fixtures/tenant-scenarios/caching.json).
- Docs: operations guide describing new defaults and rollout guidance (docs/ops/cost-optimization-guides.md).

Commits (high level):
- 9f3a2b1: initial cache defaults and config plumbing
- d7b4c88: quantization safety-layer implementation and unit tests
- 3c2d1f4: console settings and CLI unit-econ-diff command

Files changed (high level):
- runtime cache defaults and interfaces; low-risk change with clear feature gates.
- new quant safety module; inserted into model rollout path with short-circuit for tenants that opted for legacy behavior.
- console UI additions and minor UX copy.
- small CLI tool to generate unit-econ delta reports used by SRE/PM.

Testing & CI:
- Local unit tests: all new unit tests pass (coverage maintained).
- Integration: e2e quant-safety and caching fixtures added; CI runs these as part of the perf-e2e job.
- CI status: passing in this PR (perf-e2e flake fixed on second run).

Review conversation (high level):
- Ethan Park: "Thanks — can we make the default warmup window configurable per-tenant? For tenants with low QPS, the warmup threshold might be hit too slowly."
  - Author reply: "Added tenant-level override and documented expected tradeoffs in the ops doc; default remains conservative to protect quality."
- Luca Morales: "The safety_score is useful, but can we ensure we surface an actionable reason in logs when a rollout is blocked?"
  - Author reply: "Yes — telemetry event added: quant.safety.blocked with reason code and tenant id (see safety-layer). Also surfaced in console as a tooltip."
- Ava Chen: "Integration tests look good; please add a smoke check that the CLI report returns non-zero delta when candidate uses 4-bit vs baseline 16-bit."
  - Author reply: "Added smoke check; test included in perf-e2e matrix."

Rollout plan:
- Merge to main behind feature flag defaulting to conservative behavior.
- Gradually open opt-in flag for internal tenants and SRE-run experiments.
- After 2 weeks of monitoring unit-econ deltas and QoQ metrics, consider promoting opt-in to tenant default for low-risk classes.

Backward compatibility:
- Existing tenants keep previous behavior unless they opt in to the new aggressive caching/quant controls. The quant safety-layer defaults to permissive legacy behavior if a tenant explicitly set legacy_rollout=true in their optimization profile.

Merge details: squashed and merged after final sign-off from reviewers. CI green.

Notes for on-call: if you observe sudden QoL regressions in production streams after enabling aggressive opt-ins, run the CLI unit-econ-diff against the last-known-good config and the opt-in config; the diff includes tokenized sample comparisons and cost delta scores to aid rollback decisions.

Related: references ENG-2910 (sensitivity-classifier), PM-743 (defaults for tenant onboarding).
